subject: Private host certificate ownership agreement — Acme Financial
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood-inference.com>
To: Eric Barnes <eric.barnes@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private host certificate ownership agreement — Acme Financial

Hi Eric,

Thanks for the productive kickoff yesterday. Per our call, I attached a short "Certificate Ownership Template" that lays out the responsibilities split between Acme and Redwood for private hostnames used by your on-prem deployment. Key points summarized here: 

- Acme owns authoritative DNS for private zones and will grant either a zone-transfer or a temporary CSR import path for Redwood's automation.
- Redwood will run certificate issuance on behalf of Acme for private endpoints inside your VPC/OCS, using an agreed service account.
- Certificate lifecycle (renewal cadence, revocation, rotation window) is in the template. Default renewal: 45 days before expiry.
- Validation method: for private domains we recommend a controlled CSR workflow or customer-provided ACME endpoint reachable from our bootstrap: we do not rely on public DNS for private zones.

Next steps I propose:
1) Review the attached template and confirm the delegation option you prefer (zone-transfer vs. CSR upload).
2) If you pick automation, confirm an onboarding service account principal and an email for alerts.
3) We can sign the agreement electronically (DocuSign link in next email once you confirm).

Attachment: cert_ownership_template_v1.pdf (attachment)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call this week if you want to walk through the template.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood-inference.com
(415) 555-0162

From: Eric Barnes <eric.barnes@acme.com>

Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 14:05:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Private host certificate ownership agreement — Acme Financial

Vanessa — thanks, got the template and appreciate the clear split. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our infra/security teams: 

1) We prefer not to open AXFR to external IP ranges. Is it possible for Acme to upload a signed CSR bundle to a secure S3 bucket that Redwood will poll?
2) For the cert format: Acme wants per-service SANs (FQDNs scoped per tenant) rather than a wildcard. Any issues with that approach when used with Redwood's edge proxies?
3) Do you have a recommended service-account naming convention and least-privilege policy we can reference?

We aim to lock the approach this week so procurement can sign off. We will also attach a short doc of CSR requirements.

Attachment: acme_csr_requirements.docx (attachment)

Thanks,
Eric
Eric Barnes
Sr. Manager, Infrastructure — Acme Financial
eric.barnes@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Eric Barnes <eric.barnes@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood-inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:22:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Private host certificate ownership agreement — Acme Financial

Eric — quick technical follow-up from SRE/Infra: 

Thanks for the CSR doc; this is all solvable. Short answers: 

1) Upload model: yes — the secure S3 CSR-upload polling model is the recommended pattern for air-gapped/private zones where AXFR is not acceptable. Our automation supports polling an S3-compatible bucket with signed role credentials (we only read from a specific prefix). We can provide an IAM trust policy and short-lived role assumption example.

2) SAN vs wildcard: SAN-per-service is preferred for security and least privilege. Our edge proxies handle multiple SANs per cert fine; you'll want to ensure the subjectAltName list stays under 100 entries to avoid CA or client size issues. If you expect thousands of hostnames per cert, we'll recommend per-service certs.

3) Service account recommendation: we suggest a scoped principal: "redwood-acme-onboard@redwood-inference-svc" with the following least-privilege actions: s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-private-csr/prefix/* and kms:Decrypt on a specific CMK if you encrypt the uploads. We'll send a sample IAM policy and an example assume-role ARN in a follow-up.

Operational notes:
- Renewal flow: Redwood will place a renewal request 45 days prior to expiry and post a pre-rotation notice to the signed contact list. If rotation fails, we fall back to the last valid cert for 72 hours and create an incident (JV alerting).
- Revocation: immediate on request; we will also rotate affected downstream proxies within the rotation window.

Action items for Acme:
- Confirm S3 prefix and whether you want a polling cadence of 5 or 15 minutes.
- Confirm the email list for rotation alerts.
- Approve the sample IAM policy we will send.

Example assume-role policy (snippet):

  {
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDWOOD_ACCOUNT:role/redwood-acme-signer"},
        "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
        "Condition": {}
      }
    ]
  }

(We will redact the account numbers in the final doc.)

—
Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood-inference.com>

Subject: Re: Private host certificate ownership agreement — Acme Financial

Eric — great, thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Marissa's notes, we'll move forward with the S3 CSR-upload model and SAN-per-service certs. Next steps and owners: 

- Acme: create s3 prefix acme-private-csr/onboard/ and confirm polling cadence (we recommend 5 minutes).
- Acme: provide rotation contact list (security@acme.com, infra-oncall@acme.com).
- Redwood: share a least-privilege IAM policy and the temporary role ARN you will assume for reads. (Owner: Marissa)
- Redwood SRE: produce a short runbook for certificate failure modes/rollback (Owner: Jonas).

I've started a DocuSign for the short ownership agreement and attached the signed copy once countersigned. Please confirm and we'll schedule a 30-minute onboarding to exchange the IAM policy and bucket prefix.

Attachments: cert_ownership_agreement_signed.pdf (attachment)

Looking forward — assigning Jonas to create the runbook and Marissa to send the IAM sample.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
